content: This medication should not be used during pregnancy. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. This medication may reduce breast milk production, and a small amount can pass into breast milk, potentially causing undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, which can result in pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (such as rifampin and rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as blood tests for clotting factors or thyroid function, potentially causing inaccurate results. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as fainting or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Follow your doctor’s instructions for breast self-examinations and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, follow the instructions provided in the product package, as advice may vary depending on the brand and the number of doses missed. You may need to use backup birth control methods, such as condoms or spermicides, to prevent pregnancy. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Side effects may include nausea, vomiting, headache, abdominal cramps or bloating, breast tenderness, swelling of the ankles or feet (fluid retention), or weight changes. Vaginal bleeding between periods (spotting) or missed/irregular periods may occur, especially during the first few months of use. If these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you have diabetes, this medication may affect your blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar regularly and share the results with your doctor. Report symptoms of high blood sugar, such as increased thirst or urination, to your doctor immediately. Inform your doctor if you have recently undergone or will undergo surgery, or if you will be confined to a bed or chair for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots, especially when using hormonal birth control. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin (melasma), which can worsen with sunlight. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. It may take longer to become pregnant after stopping birth control pills.
